exposure: pregnancy within 24 months of renal transplantation
pregnancy more than 24 months after renal transplantation
cohort: The study included 44 patients who became pregnant following renal transplantation using living donors.
finding: A longer interval between renal transplantation and pregnancy (more than 24 months) is associated with better pregnancy outcomes, specifically higher mean gestational age and fetal birth weight, and lower proteinuria in the third trimester.
mod_finding: Normal vaginal delivery occurred in 58.3% and 55% of cases for the longer and shorter interval groups, respectively, while cesarean section was performed in 41.6% and 45% of cases, respectively.
birth_weight: Group A (pregnancy >24 months post-transplant): 2,480+/-316 g; Group B (pregnancy <24 months post-transplant): 2,284.5+/-262 g
gest_age: Group A (pregnancy >24 months post-transplant): 35.8+/-3 weeks; Group B (pregnancy <24 months post-transplant): 34.1+/-2.5 weeks
